content:

title: Getting Started with Next.js
excerpt: Next.js is a powerful React framework that makes building fast, production-ready web apps a breeze. Here's how to get started.
content:
Next.js is one of the most popular React frameworks out there, and for good reason. It gives you server-side rendering, static site generation, file-based routing, and much more — all out of the box. ## Why Next.js? Next.js takes the complexity out of building modern web applications. You get: - **File-based routing**: Create a file inside the `app` folder and it becomes a route automatically. - **Server Components**: Render components on the server by default for better performance. - **Static Generation**: Pre-render pages at build time for blazing-fast delivery. ## Your First Page Create a file at `app/page.tsx` and export a default React component. That's it — you have a page! ```tsx export default function Home() { return

title: Why JSON is Great for Small Projects
excerpt: Sometimes a database is overkill. For small blogs and side projects, a local JSON file is all you need to get things moving.
content:
Not every project needs a full database. For small blogs, portfolios, or side projects, a local JSON file can be the perfect data store.

## The Benefits

**Simple to read and write**: JSON is human-readable and easy to edit in any text editor.

**No setup required**: No databases to configure, no connection strings to manage. Just a file in your project.

**Version control friendly**: Because it's just a text file, your data lives right alongside your code in Git.

**Fast**: Reading a local file is extremely fast — no network round-trips or database queries.

## When to Move On

Of course, JSON files have limits. When your data grows large, when you need complex queries, or when multiple users need to write data simultaneously, it's time to reach for a proper database like PostgreSQL or MongoDB.

But for getting started? A JSON file is a lazy panda's best friend.
